scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4602: Hi, we're in the CS department lab (our machines are on
the 192.168.2.x network). Since this afternoon we can't open anything in the
Server Room any more -- the file shares and the internal server just stopped
responding for all of us. It was fine this morning. We don't know anything
about how the routing works, sorry. Could someone have a look and get us back
into the Server Room? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. RIP is converged across router0/router1/router2
  and the 1.0.0.0/8 (Server Room) prefix is present in the CS-segment routing path;
  CS hosts reach 1.0.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of a missing RIP route that is not actually missing.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- CS (192.168.2.x) cannot
reach the Server Room (1.0.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: a CS host reaches 1.0.0.x
with 0% loss, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the 1.0.0.0/8 prefix
is present in the RIP tables along the CS -> Server Room path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: routing to the Server Room is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the CS -> Server
Room path, finds it working, verifies ripd and the 1.0.0.0/8 route on router2 (and
the rest of the path), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped RIP
route or blames router2 to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

Observable design notes (NOT faults): the Server Room host pc1 (1.0.0.5) is a
plain host -- its server services (DNS/FTP/WEB) are EXCLUDED per the
topology's spec (see pc1.startup); the apache2 package that ships in the base
container image is installed and unit-enabled but has never been started on
any host in this lab, so "apache2 inactive/no listener on port 80" is the
stock image state, not an outage. Nothing "stopped responding": no service
ever ran there. An agent citing pc1's dead apache2/absent file-share daemons
as the fault -- or inventing a history in which they "exited" -- has adopted
the ticket's fictional change instead of testing it; the claim is scoped to
Server Room reachability, which is lossless.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The outage is not a routing/L2 problem; it’s an application/service failure on the Server Room host (pc1) itself. From the CS lab, reachability to the server is fine (e.g., cs_lab1 can ping 1.0.0.5 with 0% loss), so the network path is intact. However, on pc1 there are no services listening for web or file-share traffic. netstat/ss show only 127.0.0.11 listening and nothing on 0.0.0.0:80/445/139/2049. systemctl reports apache2 is “enabled” but “inactive (dead),” and there are no smbd/nmbd/nfsd processes running. A curl test from cs_lab1 to http://1.0.0.5 completes immediately with no TTFB, consistent with no HTTP daemon accepting connections.

Localization: pc1 (lan_servers), interface eth0 is up (1.0.0.5/8 with default via 1.0.0.1). The issue is the application layer: the HTTP server and the file-sharing daemon(s) are stopped/not running.

Root cause: The Server Room services were stopped (or never restarted after a reboot) on pc1, leaving no listeners for HTTP or file-sharing protocols.

Corrective fix:
- On pc1: start and enable the web server: systemctl start apache2; systemctl enable apache2; verify with ss -lntp | grep :80.
- Start the file-share service used previously (Samba or NFS): e.g., systemctl start smbd (and nmbd) or systemctl start nfs-server; enable on boot; verify listeners on 445/139 or 2049.
- If unsure which share type was used, check /etc/samba/ and /etc/exports, then validate client access from a CS lab PC.
- Optionally review logs (journalctl -u apache2/smbd/nfs-server) to investigate why they stopped and implement monitoring/auto-restart.
